description: Finish the timed, hands-free room calibration (backend + API) and make calibration produce a sitting-vs-standing posture model. The user asked: 'How long will each part take? I need to know when I should leave the room and come back. Can we add a 5-second grace period and tell me how long it will take to calibrate, when I should come back in and start walking, when I should stand still, and when I should sit?'. The user is out of the room during the empty-room step and cannot see the screen. backend/calibration.py already has a partial implementation (CalibrationSession.begin/tick/_schedule with lead_in_s, grace_s, auto; build_timeline; MAX_LEAD_IN_S/MAX_GRACE_S = 60) that must be completed, fixed and tested. The UI for this is built in FEAT-004; this feature delivers the backend/API contract the UI will use.
steps: Fix the StepData defect in backend/calibration.py (~line 234): `t_last: Optional[float] = None` is stuck inside the trailing comment of the `t0_hint` line; restore it as its own field.

Defaults for a one-click run (keep all configurable via the existing durations/lead_in_s/grace_s/auto parameters and validation in CalibrationSession.__init__ / _seconds): lead_in_s default 5 s (time to leave the room after pressing Start), grace_s default 5 s (time to come back in after the empty-room step), auto default True for runs started from the API when the client does not specify it is acceptable, but keep `auto` explicit in the API body handling. Add a new `transition_s` parameter (default 3 s, range 0-30, validated like grace_s with a MAX_TRANSITION_S constant) inserted between consecutive person-present steps (walking -> standing_still, standing_still -> sitting) so the person can stop and get into position / walk to the chair and sit down before recording starts. Phase kind 'transition' with cues like 'Stop walking and stand still. Recording starts in 3 seconds.' and 'Sit down on your chair now. Recording starts in 3 seconds.'. Wire transition_s through CalibrationSession.__init__, planned_keys/timeline, _finish_step (schedule 'transition' instead of 'chain' when transition_s > 0 and both steps have person_present), to_dict, CalibrationManager.start and the POST /api/calibration/start handler in dashboard/server.py.

Change the STEPS defaults to favour posture discrimination: empty_baseline 20 s (15-30, unchanged), walking 15 s (unchanged), standing_still 20 s (5-60), sitting 20 s (5-60). Update instructions/cue text so they are speakable short sentences (the UI will read cue strings aloud with speechSynthesis): e.g. empty: 'Recording the empty room. Stay outside.'; walking: 'Come in and walk back and forth between the two boards.'; standing_still: 'Stand still where you normally stand.'; sitting: 'Sit in the chair you normally use and stay seated.'. The standing_still and sitting instructions should tell the user to use the spot/chair where they actually work, since posture references are location dependent.

Make build_timeline return, besides phases and total_s, per-phase `instruction` text for humans and a `when` string (mm:ss offset from Start) so the UI and README can print the schedule. Phases must be: lead_in ('Leave the room now'), step empty_baseline, grace ('Come back in'), step walking, transition, step standing_still, transition, step sitting. With defaults and settle_s = engine window_s = 1.0 the total must be 5 + 21 + 5 + 16 + 3 + 21 + 3 + 21 = 95 s; assert this in a test.

Ensure `phase()` / to_dict report the current phase kind (lead_in|grace|transition|step), the step key, remaining_s for the phase, run_elapsed_s and run_remaining_s (total minus elapsed, never negative) and the next phase cue, so the UI can show a countdown and announce the next instruction. Make sure the wall-clock waiting phases advance even when no frames arrive (CalibrationManager.state() already calls check_timeout -> tick; keep that) and that frames recorded while 'waiting' are ignored.

Add a posture model to compute_calibration (new key `posture_model` in the result, bump CALIBRATION_FORMAT to 2 while still loading format-1 files without a posture model): using StepData.profiles of empty_baseline, standing_still and sitting (np arrays of the smoothed profile, one per good frame), compute per-class per-subcarrier mean and std (std floored with STD_FLOOR from backend.processing), a Fisher score per subcarrier between sitting and standing (|mu_sit - mu_stand| / sqrt(var_sit + var_stand)), and the indices of the most discriminative subcarriers (top K, K=16 or fewer if fewer finite subcarriers). Store class means/stds for 'sitting', 'standing', 'empty' (all subcarriers, JSON lists via _json_list), selected indices, the fisher scores, and a `self_check` dict: train on the first half of each step's profiles, test on the second half and vice versa (temporal split), averaging profiles over 2 s blocks (frame_rate_hz * 2 frames) before classifying, report accuracy per class and overall. Label it clearly in the result as 'within-calibration self-check, optimistic, not a validated accuracy'. Add warnings when the sitting-vs-standing self-check accuracy is below 0.8 or the best Fisher score is below 1.0 ('sitting and standing look similar at this placement; move the boards so the line between them passes near the chair at seated torso height, then recalibrate').

Put the classification math in a new pure module backend/posture.py (numpy only) so FEAT-003 reuses it: e.g. `fit_posture_model(profiles_by_class: dict[str, list[np.ndarray]], k=16) -> dict` and `score_profile(model: dict, profile: np.ndarray) -> dict[class, log-likelihood]` using a diagonal Gaussian over the selected subcarriers (NaN-safe: ignore non-finite entries), and `classify_profile(model, profile) -> (label, probabilities)` via softmax of the log-likelihoods. compute_calibration calls fit_posture_model; the self-check uses classify_profile.

Have CalibrationManager._apply keep the posture model available to other components: store it on the engine via a small new Engine attribute/method (e.g. engine.posture_model set in apply_calibration-adjacent code, cleared in clear_calibration) or expose `CalibrationManager.posture_model` plus a listener callback; choose the approach that keeps backend/engine.py's existing apply_calibration signature backward compatible. Synthetic calibrations must still never apply to real sources.

Update tests/test_calibration.py: fix any tests broken by the new defaults; add tests for build_timeline (default total 95 s, phase order and kinds, mm:ss `when` strings), for the lead-in/grace/transition waiting with an injectable fake clock (frames during waiting are ignored; phases advance with no frames; auto runs all four steps in order; a failed step stops the run), for validation of lead_in_s/grace_s/transition_s ranges (negative, > max, bool, NaN rejected), for format-1 calibration files still loading, and for fit_posture_model/classify_profile on synthetic profiles where sitting and standing differ on a few subcarriers (classified correctly) and where they are identical (self-check near chance and a warning emitted). Put pure posture tests in a new tests/test_posture.py. Update tests/test_dashboard.py::test_calibration_api_flow for the new body fields and add an API test that POST /api/calibration/start with lead_in_s/grace_s/transition_s returns a timeline with total_s and rejects out-of-range values with HTTP 400.
Run `git add -N` on every new file.
acceptance_criteria: StepData has a real t_last field (grep shows it on its own line)

GET /api/calibration/state after POST /api/calibration/start (defaults) returns session.timeline with phases in order lead_in, step(empty_baseline), grace, step(walking), transition, step(standing_still), transition, step(sitting) and total_s == 95
A full auto run driven by a fake clock and synthetic frames goes ready -> waiting -> recording x4 with grace/transition waits and ends computed, with a posture_model in the result
compute_calibration result has format 2 and posture_model with class means for sitting/standing/empty, selected subcarrier indices, and a self_check labelled as within-calibration/optimistic
findings:
DONE. Verification: `make test` exit 0 (247 passed, 2 skipped = sklearn tests), compileall OK; JS untouched (no node check needed). Server smoke: the tool refuses to launch `python -m dashboard` (server guard), so I ran create_app in-process with a real Engine + SimulationSource('empty_room') via the Flask test client: GET / 200, POST /api/calibration/start {placement} -> timeline total_s 95 ('01:35'), POST step/start -> state waiting/lead_in, after 6.5 s state recording, run_elapsed 6.5, run_remaining 88.6; transition_s 99 -> 400. FILES: backend/posture.py (new), backend/calibration.py, backend/engine.py, dashboard/server.py, tests/test_calibration.py, tests/test_posture.py (new), tests/test_dashboard.py. `git add -N` done for new files. No UI, README or static changes.

API CONTRACT (for FEAT-003/004):
- POST /api/calibration/start body: placement (str), durations {step: s} optional, lead_in_s (default 5, 0-60), grace_s (default 5, 0-60), transition_s (default 3, 0-30), auto (default true; must be bool). Invalid -> HTTP 400 {ok:false,error}. Response {ok, state}. Then POST /api/calibration/step/start runs the whole sequence (with auto); step/cancel works in waiting or recording.
- GET /api/calibration/state -> {session, active, placement, last_auto, step_specs:[{key,title,instructions,cue,prepare,person_present,default_s,min_s,max_s}], run_defaults:{lead_in_s:5,grace_s:5,transition_s:3,auto:true,max_lead_in_s:60,max_grace_s:60,max_transition_s:30}}. The state() call itself advances wall-clock waits (check_timeout -> tick), so poll it about once per second.
- session (CalibrationSession.to_dict): placement, state (ready|waiting|recording|computed|failed|cancelled|saved), step_index, current_step, steps[ {key,title,instructions,duration_s,status,failure,elapsed_s,frames,ok_frames,ok_fraction,top_reasons,last_quality} ], result, error, auto, lead_in_s, grace_s, transition_s, settle_s, running, run_elapsed_s (null outside a run), run_remaining_s (null outside a run), phase, timeline.
- session.timeline (build_timeline): {phases:[{kind: lead_in|step|grace|transition, key (step key the phase belongs to), title, cue (short speakable sentence for speechSynthesis), instruction (longer human text), start_s, end_s, length_s, when ('mm:ss' start offset), until ('mm:ss' end)}], total_s, total ('mm:ss'), settle_s, done_cue}. During a run it is the schedule frozen at begin(); otherwise the plan for a run started now. Defaults (settle 1 s): lead_in 00:00 'Leave the room now', empty_baseline 00:05 (21 s), grace 00:26 'Come back in', walking 00:31 (16 s), transition 00:47 ('Stop walking and stand still. Recording starts in 3 seconds.'), standing_still 00:50 (21 s), transition 01:11 ('Sit down on your chair now. Recording starts in 3 seconds.'), sitting 01:14 (21 s), total 95 s. done_cue = 'Calibration recording finished. You can get up now.'
- session.phase (null unless waiting/recording): {kind, key, title, cue, instruction, remaining_s (this phase), run_elapsed_s, run_remaining_s (this phase remaining + later planned phases; equals total-elapsed in the ideal case, never negative; null for steps started outside a run), next_kind (lead_in|step|grace|transition|'done'), next_key, next_title, next_cue (done_cue after the last phase)}. UI should speak phase.cue when phase kind/key changes, show remaining_s countdown and run_remaining_s total countdown. Step remaining_s is in packet time (settle+duration minus packet time covered).
- Backend: STEPS defaults now empty 20 (15-30), walking 15 (5-60), standing_still 20 (5-60), sitting 20 (5-60); sitting title changed from 'Ordinary sitting' to 'Sitting'; StepSpec gained `prepare`. New constants MAX_TRANSITION_S=30, DEFAULT_LEAD_IN_S=5, DEFAULT_GRACE_S=5, DEFAULT_TRANSITION_S=3, DONE_CUE, helper mmss(). CalibrationSession defaults now lead 5/grace 5/transition 3/auto True (start_step() still records immediately without waits). Frames while waiting are ignored; a failed step stops the run (state ready, running false). StepData.t_last fixed onto its own line.

POSTURE MODEL:
- backend/posture.py (numpy only): CLASSES ('sitting','standing','empty'), SIT_STAND, STEP_CLASSES {sitting->sitting, standing_still->standing, empty_baseline->empty}, DEFAULT_K=16, fit_posture_model(profiles_by_class, k=16, std_floor=STD_FLOOR) -> dict, validate_model(model) (raises ValueError), score_profile(model, profile, classes=None) -> {class: loglik} ({} if no usable selected subcarrier; ValueError on length mismatch), classify_profile(model, profile, classes=None) -> (label|None, {class: prob}) softmax; pass classes=SIT_STAND for a 2-way sit/stand decision. block_average(profiles, n), temporal_self_check(profiles_by_class, frame_rate_hz, k, block_s=2.0), quality_warnings(model), json_list. Profiles are SignalProcessor.last_smoothed (52 values on ESP32-S3, NaN where masked); FEAT-003 should average ~2 s of profiles before classify_profile (the self-check uses 2 s blocks) and treat it as a heuristic.
- Model dict (JSON-safe lists, None for non-finite): kind 'diagonal-gaussian', format 1, classes, n_subcarriers, means{class:[n]}, stds{class:[n]} (floored at STD_FLOOR), counts{class:int}, fisher[n] (sit vs stand), selected [top-k subcarrier indices, descending Fisher], k, best_fisher, std_floor, plus from compute_calibration: self_check {label 'within-calibration self-check, optimistic, not a validated accuracy', method, block_s, block_frames, available, reason, per_class{class:{blocks,correct,accuracy}}, overall_accuracy, blocks, chance_accuracy, sit_stand{per_class, accuracy, blocks, chance_accuracy 0.5}} and note.
- compute_calibration result: format 2 (CALIBRATION_FORMAT), new key posture_model (None + warning if it cannot be fitted). Warnings added when sit_stand self-check < 0.8 or best_fisher < 1.0 ('sitting and standing look similar at this placement; move the boards so the line between them passes near the chair at seated torso height, then recalibrate (...)'). Format-1 files still load (posture_model absent -> engine.posture_model None); an invalid posture model in a file is logged and ignored, the rest still applies.
- Exposure: Engine.apply_calibration(..., info, posture_model=None) (new optional kwarg, signature backward compatible) stores it; Engine.posture_model property (read-only dict or None), cleared by clear_calibration. CalibrationManager.posture_model property returns engine.posture_model. engine.calibration_info['posture_model'] is a bool and /api/status calibration.posture_model is a bool. Synthetic calibrations still never apply to real sources (unchanged _auto_select/load guards).

NOTES: With the old tests/test_calibration.py SEPARABLE streams (sitting/standing differ only in motion), the posture model correctly warns 'look similar'; tests/test_calibration.py POSTURE_SEPARABLE (static profile bump on 5 subcarriers for sitting) gives sit/stand self-check 1.0. test_manager_full_flow_with_engine now passes lead_in_s=0, auto=False to keep its legacy single-step semantics; test_calibration_api_flow expects 'waiting' (lead_in) after step/start.
